question: Assume today is 2026-10-19. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of tokens per minute that Alphabet's first-party models (such as Gemini) process via direct API use by customers, as it will be first stated with Alphabet's third-quarter 2026 results (earnings press release or CEO earnings-call remarks); in Q2 2026 Alphabet stated this as 'Gemini models now process 22 billion API tokens per minute'. Answer in tokens per minute.

target.what: Rate at which Alphabet's first-party models (e.g. Gemini) process tokens via direct API use by customers, as first disclosed with Alphabet's Q3 2026 results (earnings release or CEO earnings-call remarks); the analogous Q2 2026 disclosure was 'Gemini models now process 22 billion API tokens per minu
target.publisher: Alphabet Inc. (earnings press release / CEO earnings-call remarks)
target.caveats: Working interpretation: the figure is a point-in-time run-rate (tokens per minute) as of the Q3 2026 disclosure, covering worldwide direct API consumption of Alphabet first-party models (Gemini family), not consumer app usage, not Vertex partner-model traffic, and not Workspace/AI Overviews internal

candidates.perspective: Alphabet investor-relations disclosures and CEO earnings-call transcripts
candidates.hypothesis: The Q3 2026 figure is the next point in a quarterly run-rate series (e.g. prior disclosures of tokens per minute at successive earnings). Fitting the recent trajectory (level and quarter-over-quarter growth) and extrapolating one quarter gives a direct estimate; growth has been rapid and possibly decelerating, so the recent growth rate is the key input.
candidates.data_to_find: All Alphabet earnings-release or earnings-call statements of 'X billion API tokens per minute' (or tokens processed) for each quarter from the first disclosure through Q2 2026, with exact dates and wording; note whether each is a run-rate or period figure. Minimum evidence: at least the last 3-4 quarterly values to estimate level and growth.

Google Q2 2026 earnings Gemini 22 billion tokens per minute
Sundar Pichai Gemini tokens processed per minute quarterly

candidates.perspective: Google Cloud / Vertex AI and Gemini API usage disclosures
candidates.hypothesis: Alphabet also discloses related usage metrics (API calls, Vertex AI usage, Cloud backlog, AI model token volumes, developer counts). These broader or adjacent totals can be bridged to the token rate via a share or conversion (e.g. tokens per API call, share of tokens via direct API vs Vertex). Direction: related totals should grow similarly, constraining the plausible range.
candidates.data_to_find: Any Alphabet/Google disclosures of Gemini API request volumes, Vertex AI customer/usage counts, tokens processed totals, or developer adoption metrics for 2025-2026; also third-party estimates of Gemini API traffic. Minimum evidence: one related volume series with a stated or inferable conversion to tokens per minute.

candidates.perspective: TPU/GPU compute capacity and inference utilisation
candidates.hypothesis: Token throughput is bounded by Alphabet's deployed inference compute (TPUs/GPUs), utilisation, and tokens per chip-second. Estimating installed AI accelerator capacity, share devoted to first-party Gemini inference, utilisation, and tokens/sec per chip gives an independent physical upper bound and central estimate.
candidates.data_to_find: Alphabet TPU deployment estimates (units, generations), capex and data-center capacity disclosures, tokens-per-second-per-TPU benchmarks for Gemini-class models, and any stated inference share of compute. Minimum evidence: an accelerator count estimate plus a tokens/sec-per-chip benchmark and utilisation assumption.

Minimum evidence: a developer count and a tokens-per-developer estimate or API revenue and price per token.

methods.label: m1

p1.role: Q2 2026 tokens per minute via direct API use (22B), the last observed run-rate

a1.role: growth factor from Q2 2026 to Q3 2026 run-rate

methods.rationale: Extrapolates the last observed direct-API token rate (p1, 22B) one quarter forward using a decelerating QoQ growth factor grounded in the 7→10→16→22B trajectory. Shared dependency: relies on p1 being the correct scope (direct API, first-party Gemini) and on growth continuing rather than reversing.

methods.label: m2

p82.role: I/O 2026 (May 2026) mid-Q2 tokens per minute reading of 19B

a2.role: growth factor from May 2026 to Q3 2026 run-rate

methods.rationale: Independent anchor using the mid-Q2 I/O reading (p82, 19B) grown through Q3 by a monthly-compounding factor. Provides a cross-check on m1 that does not start from the Q2 endpoint. Failure mode: if the 19B I/O figure used a different scope than the earnings disclosures, this route is biased.

kept.name: Q3 2026 vs Q2 2026 token-rate growth factor

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
